spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m4p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers
VARIABLES holders, queue, cap
Init == holders = 0 /\ queue = 0 /\ cap = 2
Grab == holders = 0 /\ holders' = (holders) + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cap>>
Release == holders > 0 /\ holders' = holders - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cap>>
Enqueue == queue < cap /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, cap>>
Drain == queue > 0 /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, cap>>
Reconfig == \E c \in {2, 3} : c >= queue /\ cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, queue>>
Next == Grab \/ Release \/ Enqueue \/ Drain \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<holders, queue, cap>>
ExclusiveDownlink == holders >= 0 /\ holders <= 1 /\ queue >= 0 /\ queue <= cap
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ExclusiveDownlink
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares a single satellite downlink channel that only one drone may transmit on at a time. Incoming imagery tasks pile into a bounded work queue; drones enqueue new tasks only while the queue has room, and the ground station drains tasks one at a time. Because smoke conditions vary, the operator can reconfigure the queue capacity up or down at runtime, but never below the number of tasks already waiting. A drone grabs the downlink only when it is free and releases it when its burst finishes. The safety concern is that two drones must never be transmitting on the shared downlink simultaneously.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at no reachable state do two drones hold the shared downlink channel at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m0p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Commit == cachedOk = TRUE /\ epoch < 4 /\ epoch' = (epoch) + 1 /\ accepted' = accepted + 1 /\ cachedOk' = FALSE
Stale == cachedOk = FALSE /\ cachedOk' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, accepted>>
Next == Read \/ Commit \/ Stale
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, accepted, cachedOk>>
OnlyCurrentEpochWrites == accepted = epoch
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyCurrentEpochWrites
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm writes consolidated maps to a shared store using optimistic locking with retry. Each write carries the epoch the drone believes is current; the store bumps its epoch on every accepted write, and the operator may grow the mission's epoch capacity at runtime as new drones join. A drone reads the store epoch, prepares a write, then commits only if its cached epoch still equals the store epoch, otherwise it retries with a fresh read. The count of accepted writes must always equal the store epoch, because every accepted write advances the epoch exactly once. The hazard is a stale drone committing under an old epoch and silently overwriting newer data.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of accepted writes always equals the store's current epoch, so no stale-epoch write is ever accepted.

nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper routes waiting passengers through a bounded dispatch queue with backpressure: passengers move from the lobby pool into cars, and cars later discharge them at their floors, but no passenger is ever created or lost in transit. New boarding requests are admitted only while a car has spare room. One car controller can crash silently and simply stop accepting boardings, but the passengers it already holds remain accounted for. Across every step the total number of people equals those still in the lobby plus those currently riding. The safety concern is strict conservation of people.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the count of people in the lobby plus the count riding in cars always equals the fixed building population.

The number of provisioned hubs can grow at runtime as the household adds devices. Only the current leader may fire the unlock, and once the door has been unlocked that irreversible pulse must never be issued a second time in the session. Leadership can hand off, but the fired flag persists across handoffs. The safety concern is that the irreversible unlock happens at most once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the master-unlock pulse is fired at most once across the whole session, regardless of leader failover.

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyLeaderRoutes
nl:
An airport baggage router elects one leader controller to divert bags onto the sortation belt; a standby is elected on failover. Two independent baggage systems share one physical belt pool, so their leaders are drawn from a common set of controller ids, and a diversion is authorized only when it comes from the controller that is currently the leader. A stale controller that believes it is still leader must never route a bag. Every routed bag increments the count of authorized routings, which must never exceed the count of diversions the true leader performed. The hazard is a deposed controller routing bags it is no longer authorized to route.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no controller other than the current leader ever performs a bag routing.

The hazard is the same output slot being allocated twice.

The hazard is exceeding the bounded shelf capacity.

A subway signalling block system records each block's occupancy with optimistic locking and retry. A train controller reads a block's version, computes its update, and commits only if the version is unchanged, bumping the version and applying the update atomically; the number of committed updates must equal the version. The line can add signalling blocks at runtime, growing capacity. A stale commit whose read version no longer matches is rejected and retried, so no update is ever lost or applied out of order. Each accepted commit advances committed count and version together. The hazard is a lost update where the version and the applied-update count drift apart.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the count of applied block updates always equals the record's version, so no committed update is ever lost.

nl:
A library book-reservation system tracks the fixed number of physical copies of a title using a compare-and-swap register on the availability count. One reservation agent can be slow but never fails, so a pending swap always eventually resolves. The register guarantees each swap either fully applies or not at all. The hazard is a bookkeeping error that creates or loses a copy.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of available copies plus the number of reserved copies always equals the fixed total of copies owned.

The hazard is the irreversible emergency brake firing more than once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the emergency-brake alarm is tripped at most once for the incident.

DispenseSlotExclusive == slot >= 0 /\ slot <= 1 /\ votes >= 0 /\ votes <= 3
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispenseSlotExclusive
nl:
A vending-machine network coordinates access to a shared refill slot through quorum voting: a technician may claim the slot only after collecting a majority of votes from the network's controllers. One controller can be slow but never fails, so a quorum is always eventually reachable. A claim needs at least a majority of the three controllers voting yes, and only then does the technician take exclusive control of the refill slot. At most one technician holds the slot at once. The hazard is two technicians holding the shared refill slot at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared refill slot is held by at most one technician at any time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m3p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers
VARIABLES leader, prints, authPrints
Init == leader = 1 /\ prints = 0 /\ authPrints = 0
Failover == \E e \in {1, 2} : leader' = e /\ UNCHANGED <<prints, authPrints>>
PrintByLeader == prints < 5 /\ prints' = (prints) + 1 /\ authPrints' = authPrints + 1 /\ UNCHANGED leader
Next == Failover \/ PrintByLeader
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<leader, prints, authPrints>>
OnlyLeaderPrints == prints = authPrints
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyLeaderPrints
nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction elects one leader matching engine to print the single opening cross; a standby is elected on failover. Two independent auction instances share one order pool, so their leaders come from a shared id set, and a cross-print is authorized only from the controller that is currently leader. A deposed engine that still believes it leads is stale and must not print. Every accepted print is by the true leader, so total prints equals leader-authorized prints. The hazard is a stale engine printing a cross it is not authorized to print.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no matching engine other than the current leader ever prints a cross.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m9p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers
VARIABLES codes, epoch
Init == codes = 0 /\ epoch = 0
Provision == codes < 4 /\ codes' = (codes) + 1 /\ UNCHANGED epoch
Revoke == codes > 0 /\ codes' = codes - 1 /\ UNCHANGED epoch
Rotate == epoch < 3 /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ UNCHANGED codes
Next == Provision \/ Revoke \/ Rotate
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<codes, epoch>>
BoundNeverExceeded == codes >= 0 /\ codes <= 4
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BoundNeverExceeded
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network provisions guest access codes into a shared code slot pool under epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a hub bumps the epoch whenever it rotates keys. Two independent hub instances share one code-slot pool, so both may provision, but the number of active codes must never exceed the pool's fixed capacity. Provisioning adds a code only while a slot is free; revocation frees a slot. Reconfiguration advances the epoch but not the physical slot capacity. The hazard is exceeding the bounded pool of code slots.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of active guest codes never exceeds the fixed code-slot pool capacity.
